# Vivado Block Design clamp

**Vendor IP is instantiated as catalog IP in a Block Design, generated by Tcl.**
Not hand-rolled in RTL, not stitched together with `create_bd_cell -type module`
around your own Verilog.

The reason is concrete rather than stylistic: catalog IP arrives with correct
interface metadata — typed clock and reset pins, `FREQ_HZ`, bundled AXI
interfaces — and a whole class of silent block-design failures simply does not
exist for it. A hand-rolled module cell has none of that, and the failures it
produces surface far from their cause.

IP catalog with known-good configurations:
[`../docs/07-vendored-ip-catalog.md`](../docs/07-vendored-ip-catalog.md).
Runnable snippets: [`../examples/bd/`](../examples/bd/).

## The clamp

**MUST: use catalog IP for anything the catalog already does.** The recurring
case is clock generation: use `xilinx.com:ip:clk_wiz:6.0`, never a hand-written
`MMCME4_ADV` module. This was a real review correction, not a hypothetical. The
underlying primitive is still reachable for a LOC constraint — clk_wiz names it
`mmcme4_adv_inst` — so you lose nothing.

**MUST: source the validated snippet rather than re-deriving.** The HBM
subsystem, the per-channel conversion path, and the boundary guard ring are
solved problems with configurations that took multiple failed builds to find.
[`hbm-subsystem.tcl`](../examples/bd/hbm-subsystem.tcl),
[`boundary-guard-ring.tcl`](../examples/bd/boundary-guard-ring.tcl).

## Four Tcl footguns

All four are **silent at the point of the mistake** and surface later with error
text that points somewhere else. Check against them before writing BD Tcl.

### 1. BD object handles do not survive storage and re-expansion

`get_bd_ports` / `get_bd_pins` return a rich Tcl object, not a string — even
though it prints and `llength`s like one. Round-tripping it through an array and
re-expanding later fails:

```tcl
lappend arr($k) [get_bd_ports $name]        ;# ... later ...
connect_bd_net ... {*}$arr($k)
# ERROR: [Common 17-161] Invalid option value '/portname' specified for 'objects'
```

which reads like a typo, not an object-lifetime problem.

**Fix: store plain name strings, resolve fresh at the point of use** —
`get_bd_ports $names` inline as a direct argument to the consuming command.

### 2. `get_bd_ports` / `get_bd_pins` take ONE list, not multiple positional args

```tcl
get_bd_ports {*}{name1 name2}   ;# ERROR: [Common 17-165] Too many positional options
get_bd_ports {name1 name2}      ;# correct
```

Easy to get backwards coming from `get_cells`, which does accept multiple
patterns.

### 3. A module cell's pins are `TYPE=undef`, and `FREQ_HZ` silently no-ops

`create_bd_cell -type module -reference <mod>` gives pins with no clock
metadata. `TYPE` is **read-only after creation** (`set_property TYPE clk` errors
outright), and `set_property CONFIG.FREQ_HZ N` on an undef pin **succeeds with
no effect** — no error, empty readback. It looks like it worked.

The symptom appears several hops downstream:

```
ERROR: [BD 41-237] Bus Interface property FREQ_HZ does not match
       between /some/unrelated/ip and /another/unrelated/ip
```

naming IPs you never touched.

**Fix, if a hand-rolled RTL module cell is genuinely unavoidable:** annotate the
Verilog source *before* the cell is created:

```verilog
(* X_INTERFACE_INFO = "xilinx.com:signal:clock:1.0 <pinname> CLK" *)
(* X_INTERFACE_PARAMETER = "FREQ_HZ <hz>" *)
output wire <pinname>;
```

Reset-like pins (`*_n`) auto-infer as `xilinx.com:signal:reset:1.0` with no
attribute. Only clocks need the annotation.

**Better fix: don't hand-roll it.** See the clamp above.

### 4. A bundled interface's physical pins have a different prefix than you expect

To tie off `hbm_0/SAXI_01`, its constituent pins are named
`hbm_0/AXI_01_ARVALID` — **not** `SAXI_01_ARVALID`. The interface pin's own name
is not the physical-pin prefix.

**Fix: always enumerate first.**

```tcl
get_bd_pins -of_objects [get_bd_intf_pins hbm_0/SAXI_01]
```

Doing this correctly also means you can tie off straight to the cell's own pins
with `xlconstant`s and never create an external "null master" port.

## Tie-offs

**MUST: drive every RP boundary output.** An undriven output synthesises to a
constant and collides with the static side's driver after the link:
`DRC MDRV-1`, hundreds of flip-flop outputs and GND driving the same net. This
includes `m_axibr` if you never write to host memory, and the unused AXI-MM
slaves. `RUN=0` does not catch it.

**MUST: null-tie unused HBM SAXI ports.** An enabled memory controller's second
pseudo-channel still needs a legally idle AXI3 master, or the controller stalls.
`vnd_hbm_null_tie` in
[`hbm-subsystem.tcl`](../examples/bd/hbm-subsystem.tcl) does it. Expect benign
`BD 41-1306` "connection overridden" warnings.

## Boundary slices

**MUST: match `rp_blk.v`'s signal set exactly.** `HAS_REGION 0` and
`SUPPORTS_NARROW_BURST 1` on the AXI-MM ports; `HAS_PROT 0` and `HAS_WSTRB 0` on
`s_axil`; `TID_WIDTH 16`, `TDEST_WIDTH 16`, `TUSER_WIDTH 32` on the streams. A
mismatch breaks the abstract-shell link and, again, `RUN=0` does not catch it
because nothing is synthesised. **Verify against
[`../libs/shell/rp_blk.v`](../libs/shell/rp_blk.v), not against a sibling
design's comment header** — several of those are stale.

**MUST: keep boundary slice cell names stable.** The guard pblocks in the XDC
select cells by name glob (`*rp_user_i*axi_regsl_dma*`). Rename in both places or
not at all. A silent zero-match wastes a 3-hour build.

## Infrastructure IP

**MUST NOT: trade a SmartConnect's mode or outstanding-transaction depth for
timing.** Relieve congestion by floorplanning
([05](05-floorplanning-and-timing.md)). Shrinking infrastructure IP costs
throughput and usually does not close timing anyway.

**MUST: set `CONFIG.ARB_ON_MAX_XFERS {0}` on an `axis_switch` using
`ARB_ON_TLAST`.** Leaving it at the IP default of 1 makes the switch
re-arbitrate every *beat*: measured 60 Mpps against 82.2 offered for 128 B
packets, plus beat-interleaving corruption when two sources target one master.
See [`../docs/07-vendored-ip-catalog.md`](../docs/07-vendored-ip-catalog.md).

**SHOULD: cross the clock before changing the data width**, and put a register
slice on the far side of the CDC. In the HBM path that `slice_b` stage is
load-bearing — without it TNS blew up to roughly −880 ns.

**SHOULD: use REG modes 10/15 only on real SLR crossings.** They mandate LAGUNA
primitives; on a path that does not cross an SLR they add a hop and make timing
worse. Light config elsewhere: `REG_AR/AW/B = 7`, `REG_R/W = 1` or `7`.

## Validating

```bash
make app BOARD=au50 APP=<app> PROJ=<name> SHELL_PKG=<zip> RUN=0
```

`RUN=0` creates the project and validates the block design without synthesis
(it forces the job count to 0). Minutes, not hours. Run it after every BD edit.
Just remember what it does *not* check: boundary slice configuration, tie-offs,
and anything else that needs synthesis or the link.

`RUN` is the switch and it **defaults to 0** — so `RUN=1` is what you need for a
real build, and a command that sets only `NTHRD` validates and exits no matter
how large the thread count looks. See
[`../docs/14-build-and-load-flow.md`](../docs/14-build-and-load-flow.md).

## Before you build

- [ ] No hand-rolled RTL for anything catalog IP provides.
- [ ] No BD object handles stored in variables and re-expanded.
- [ ] `get_bd_*` called with a single list argument.
- [ ] Interface physical pins enumerated with `-of_objects`, not guessed.
- [ ] Every boundary output driven; unused HBM SAXI null-tied.
- [ ] Boundary slice configs checked against `rp_blk.v`.
- [ ] Slice cell names match the XDC globs.
- [ ] `ARB_ON_MAX_XFERS 0` wherever `ARB_ON_TLAST` is set.
- [ ] `RUN=0` validates.
